thread:
rachel: Heads up0: new model 'hera-liteq' onboarded to canary. initial structured-output smoke shows ~2.4% JSON schema noncompliance for toolcall-v3 across int4 quantized variant. noncompliance means parse errors or extra trailing tokens. anyone else seeing this?
sam: yup saw the canary dashboard spike. quick diff vs float32 baseline shows most failures are missing closing brace or an extra null byte (\u0000) before the final object.
leo: extra null byte smells like a buffer/stream chunk alignment problem when microbatching + kv rehydrate. int4 path uses smaller emit buffers, so when a streaming chunk boundary hits mid-escape sequence we can leak a NUL into output.
priya: repro tests? can we get a minimal prompt that reliably reproduces fail? also what's the failure distribution across prompts (long vs short)?
rachel: repro in thread:```
User: invoke_tool search("inference runtime kernels")
Model out: {"action":"search","args":{"query":"inference runtime kernels"},
\u0000
```
(that trailing NUL seems to break the downstream JSON parser)
sam: interesting. eval-bot, can you run a paired canary run: variants int4,int8,fp32; toggles: streaming on/off, kv_reuse on/off; sample=1k per cell. record parse_fail_count, schema_invalid_count, and percent_malformed_suffix. tag results by prompt length bucket.
eval-bot: queued job 9123. estimated runtime ~30m. will post aggregated CSV here when done.
leo: in the meantime, fast mitigation options: 1) add output sanitization post-step to strip trailing control chars and attempt parse-repair; 2) special-case canary route to disable streaming for int4 only; 3) add sentinel byte (e.g., "\uE000" private use) appended server-side before streaming, then strip in postprocess and assert validity. pros/cons?
priya: 1 and 3 are both viable. #1 is easiest but might mask real regressions; #3 is safer for canary because it makes truncation explicit. we can append sentinel then the client-side parser can check presence, attempt repair, and if sentinel missing mark as truncated.
sam: +1 for sentinel in canary only. also add tokenizer token-offset logs for failing traces (last 48 token ids and byte offsets). we need to see whether the null comes from tokenizer or post-tokenization buffer.
rachel: i'll spin up a mirror with sentinel append + token-offset probe. will route only canary traffic and add metric 'sentinel_missing_rate'. pushing in 10m.
eat: small but important note: make sure our streaming codec doesn't compress newlines out; i noticed earlier we sometimes collapse repeated whitespace on kernel A which can nudge escape sequences. check kernel flags `compact_output=true` in compiled profile.
leo: good catch. add check in bisect matrix for compiled kernel selector (kernelA/kernelB) too. streaming + kernelA + int4 sounds suspect.
eval-bot: job 9123 completed. summary (csv uploaded to /canary/jobs/9123/report.csv). top-level numbers: int4-streaming-true-kvtrue parse_fail_rate=2.41%, sentinel_missing=94% of fails; int8-streaming-true-kvtrue parse_fail_rate=0.22%; fp32-streaming-true-kvtrue parse_fail_rate=0.05%. disabling streaming on int4 -> parse_fail_rate=0.36%.
priya: looks pretty clearly streaming+int4+microbatch combo. next steps: A) keep sentinel experiment enabled for 48h B) implement server-side streaming chunk boundary fix in kernelB and recompile C) rerun canary with token-offset debug to verify no NUL insertion.
sam: also add CI gate: if canary parse_fail_rate > 0.5% for toolcall-v3 on any new quant variant, block auto-rollout.
rachel: agreed. i'll draft a short runbook for oncall: detection alerts, rollback flag, and canary toggles. will post PR for sentinel patch and runbook shortly.
leo: if kernel fix is nontrivial, we might also consider microquant retrain to avoid pathological activation ranges causing mid-escape tokens, but that's last resort.
priya: thanks all. once kernelB builds land i'll queue a follow-up canary run. :rocket:
